ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows triangle ABC with B and C on the base BC, A above them, F marked on side AC, segment BF drawn, G marked on BF, and line AG meeting side BC at E. Reasoning: Use an affine-coordinate setup, since affine transformations preserve collinearity and ratios along a line, including midpoints. Choose convenient coordinates B=(0,0), C=(1,0), and A=(0,h). Given AF:FC=1:2, point F is one-third of the way from A to C, so F = A + (1/3)(C-A) = (1/3, 2h/3). Since G is the midpoint of BF, G = ((0+1/3)/2, (0+2h/3)/2) = (1/6, h/3). The line through A=(0,h) and G=(1/6,h/3) has slope (h/3-h)/(1/6-0) = -4h, so its equation is y = h - 4hx. It meets BC where y=0, giving 0 = h - 4hx, hence x=1/4. Thus E=(1/4,0). Therefore BE:EC = 1/4 : 3/4 = 1:3.
